content:
Dating reality shows have always been a hugely popular genre that Apple TV has never ventured into. Although its newly announced series "The Last Person on Earth" is positioned as a "documentary series" rather than a "reality show," it is still the streaming platform's very first dating show.

"The Last Person on Earth" will invite renowned couples therapist Esther Perel to participate in this "innovative experiment"

Esther Perel is a well-known couples therapist and a New York Times bestselling author who specializes in the field of interpersonal relationships.

Perel is also the central figure of the newly announced 8-episode dating documentary series "The Last Person on Earth" on Apple TV.

The press release states: "In this series, couples who appear to be complete opposites on the surface will be carefully matched by Perel and a team of matchmaking experts and therapists, before embarking on an adventure together to some of the world's most romantic and remote destinations."

It sounds like a reality show, but without the negative connotations that come with the reality show brand itself. I suspect Apple's approach to this dating series is designed to create a sense of "prestige," which is why they're using the "documentary series" label.

Here's Perel herself introducing the show:

There's no premiere date set for the series yet, but it's likely to debut sometime in 2027.

Speaking of which, Apple announced yesterday that it will adapt bestselling author Rebecca Yarros's latest romance novel into a TV series. It seems clear that the streaming platform is looking to expand its business beyond its current core genres of sci-fi, comedy, and thriller.

Apple TV costs $12.99 per month, or you can get a discount by bundling it through an Apple One subscription.
